title: Tech Note: 4D Office Library
author: Silvio Belini, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D Office Library component generating Office Open XML (.docx/.xlsx) via DOM XML commands
Command-line zip (Mac) / 7-zip (Windows) invoked via LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS to package OOXML containers
VBScript (cscript) / AppleScript (osascript) bridges for Outlook and Address Book contact/appointment import-export
Drag-and-drop field-binding GUI on output forms for Word/Excel/Outlook integration

historical_commentary.text: This note documents a component that hand-builds Office Open XML (.docx/.xlsx) documents by manually constructing the required XML parts with 4D DOM commands, then shelling out to zip/7-zip via LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS to package them, and bridges to Outlook/Address Book by generating and executing VBScript/AppleScript files. This entire approach reflects the pre-native-document-generation era of 4D: modern 4D has since gained native, built-in facilities for generating spreadsheets and rich documents (4D Write Pro and 4D View Pro, ~v16-18) without hand-rolled OOXML/zip plumbing, and calling out to VBScript/AppleScript for Outlook/Contacts integration is a fragile OS-automation technique that has been largely superseded by native calendar/contacts APIs, dedicated connectors, or REST-based integrations. The component's manual XML/zip approach and OS-scripting bridges are best regarded as historical technique rather than current best practice.
related_updates: 4D Write Pro / 4D View Pro (4D v16-18+) provide native document/spreadsheet generation, removing the need to hand-build Office Open XML and shell out to zip utilities
Modern integration with Outlook/Exchange/calendars now favors REST/Graph APIs or dedicated connectors over generated VBScript/AppleScript automation
